definitions.explanation: The mathematical operation of rounding a number to the nearest whole number or specified decimal place. Literally means 'discard four, enter five' — values below five are rounded down and values of five or above are rounded up.

examples.japanese: {小数点|しょうすうてん}{以下|いか}を{四捨五入|ししゃごにゅう}する。
3.7を{四捨五入|ししゃごにゅう}すると4になる。
{計算|けいさん}{結果|けっか}は{四捨五入|ししゃごにゅう}して{整数|せいすう}で{答|こた}えなさい。
examples.english: Round the calculation result and give the answer as a whole number.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Literally "{四|し}を{捨|す}て{五|ご}を{入|い}れる" — discard (round down) at four, include (round up) at five. This four-character compound elegantly describes the standard rounding rule.

GRAMMAR:
Used with する to form a verb: {四捨五入|ししゃごにゅう}する (to round off).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {四捨五入|ししゃごにゅう}する (to round off)
- {小数点|しょうすうてん}{以下|いか}を{四捨五入|ししゃごにゅう}する (to round off decimal places)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {切|き}り{上|あ}げ: rounding up
- {切|き}り{捨|す}て: rounding down, truncation
